lesson_title: Reasons Are Marks: Paper Two Essentials
hook_text: In circle geometry, a CORRECT answer with no reason can score nothing. The marks are paid in words.
clip_script: Euclidean geometry pays its marks in a currency of reasons: every statement in a proof earns only when its reason is stated in the accepted wording. A central angle of one hundred and forty degrees forces seventy degrees at the circumference — reason, angle at centre equals two times angle at circumference. A diameter whispers ninety degrees. A tangent whispers tan-chord. A cyclic quadrilateral whispers supplementary. Riders are solved backwards and forwards at once: mark everything given, because each given is a theorem invitation, then read the target and ask what would prove it. The proof is the corridor where the two searches meet — written statement by statement, each with its reason, no steps assumed.
visual_style: A dim circle diagram where each stated reason switches on a lamp over one angle; wrong or missing reasons leave the lamp dark until the whole figure glows.
mood: Detective procedural — every claim needs its evidence.
pacing: Slow lamp-by-lamp build, quickening as the whispers stack, full glow on the final reason.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision sweep and learn the wording that switches the lamps on.
